$comment: MACHINE-READABLE ATTRIBUTE DELTA for the FlowX onboarding spec, v1.3.0 -> v1.4.0. Intended to be fed directly to an automated agent updating the Databricks App (databricks-app/) or any other spec-authoring surface. Every path below is expressed as it appears in an onboarding spec document, rooted at the spec object; `[]` denotes an array element. This file is hand-authored and is the source of truth for the delta; the enforcing artefacts are onboarding_templates/onboarding_spec.schema.json (structure) and src/flowx/lakeflow_framework/onboarding/spec_validator.py (semantics, including the rejection messages quoted below verbatim).

summary.migration_required_for: Any spec declaring a removed attribute, or cdc_load_strategy FULL_SNAPSHOT_CDC_NO_PK. Onboarding REJECTS these rather than ignoring them, so a stale spec fails loudly at onboarding time and never reaches a pipeline run.

added.default_behaviour: When absent, the framework uses the Spark type it observes for the column at encryption time. This is exactly the pre-v1.4.0 behaviour, so no existing spec needs editing and no spec is invalidated by the addition.
added.ui_position: Immediately after `mode` and before `secret`, inside the encrypted_columns[] repeat group.
added.description: The original source data type of the column being encrypted, before AES encryption replaces its physical type with ciphertext binary.
added.rationale: The captured type becomes the Unity Catalog `original_data_type` column tag, which is what a downstream `transformation_flows[].source_inputs[].decrypted_columns[].cast_to_type` is validated against at decryption time. With no declaration, whatever the source happens to deliver today becomes the tag -- so a source column that quietly changes from string to int silently re-tags, and the DECRYPT side starts failing later, far from the cause. With a declaration, the disagreement is caught at encryption time, naming both types.

validation.onboarding: Type-checked only (non-empty string). The declared value is a Spark type string; the validator has no Spark session to parse it and no source schema to check it against.
validation.runtime: crypto/column_crypto.py::apply_aes_column_encryption compares the declared value against the column's actual Spark dtype, case-insensitively and whitespace-trimmed. A mismatch raises CryptoError naming both. It does not pick a winner.
validation.runtime_error_message: encrypted_columns source_data_type mismatch for column '<col>': the spec declares source_data_type=<declared> but Spark reports <observed> for this column. Either the source's type changed, or the declaration is stale. Fix: correct source_data_type to <observed>, or remove it to accept whatever the source delivers.

added.app_action: Add a text field to the encrypted_columns[] repeat group. Optional, no default value, blank means omit the key from the serialized spec entirely (do not emit an empty string).

removed.trigger: PRESENCE, not truthiness -- `false` is rejected too, because it still describes a feature that no longer exists.
removed.rejection_message: source_config.normalize_column_names: removed in v1.4.0 -- column_normalization is now the only switch. Replace normalize_column_names: true with column_normalization: {enabled: true} (add a case key if you were relying on something other than the default 'lower'); delete the key outright if it was false.
removed.migration_trap: Before v1.4.0 a column_normalization object that OMITTED `enabled` deferred enablement to this boolean, so {"case": "preserve"} alone was ON. It now reads as written: OFF. A spec relying on that deferral must add an explicit "enabled": true or it silently stops renaming.
removed.app_action: Remove the boolean field from the Source step. Remove `normalize_column_names` from the visibility condition on `column_normalization.case` -- it must now depend on `column_normalization.enabled === true` alone. On spec IMPORT, surface the key as a migration warning rather than silently dropping it.

removed.rejection_message: target_config.generate_surrogate_key: removed in v1.4.0 -- the surrogate-key engine is gone. __framework_surrogate_key is no longer generated for any flow. Declare real primary_keys (SCD1/SCD2/SCD3/FULL_SNAPSHOT_CDC all take them), or use TRUNCATE_AND_LOAD if this source has no key.
removed.app_action: Remove the boolean field from the Load strategy step. Remove any derived 'surrogate key' feature chip from template/preset summaries.

removed.rejection_message: target_config.surrogate_key_columns: removed in v1.4.0 with the surrogate-key engine -- it scoped a column that is no longer generated. To control what identifies a row, set primary_keys; to control what is compared for change, set columns_to_check/columns_to_exclude.
removed.app_action: Remove the list field from the Load strategy step.

removed.rejection_message: target_config.surrogate_key_exclude_columns: removed in v1.4.0 with the surrogate-key engine -- it scoped a column that is no longer generated. To control what identifies a row, set primary_keys; to control what is compared for change, set columns_to_check/columns_to_exclude.
removed.app_action: Remove the list field from the Load strategy step. Also remove the former cross-field validation rule 'surrogate_key_exclude_columns must not overlap surrogate_key_columns'.

removed.trigger: PRESENCE. BOTH former values are rejected, including "triggered" -- it is removed as an ATTRIBUTE, so a spec asserting the surviving behaviour still names a field that no longer exists.
removed.rejection_message: reconciliation_flow[<id>].recon_mode: removed in v1.4.0 -- reconciliation is triggered-only. Every run is a bounded job task: batch reads, and trigger(availableNow=True) for a read_mode 'streaming' side, so the run drains its backlog and finishes. There is no continuous reconciliation mode and no recon_mode widget; delete the key. For continuous coverage, schedule the reconciliation job on the cadence you need.
removed.replacement_behaviour: Triggered semantics are now unconditional. To reconcile more often, schedule the reconciliation job more often.
removed.app_action: Remove the select field from the Reconciliation identity section. Remove `recon_mode` from every reconciliation template/preset body.

removed.rejection_message: reconciliation_flow[<id>].generate_surrogate_key: removed in v1.4.0 with the surrogate-key engine. A reconciliation flow matches on its declared match_keys; both sides must carry those columns.
removed.app_action: Remove the boolean field from the Matching & healing section.

enum_values_removed.note_scd3: SCD3 remains transformation_flows-only; it is a hard error on any ingestion_flows entry. That is unchanged in v1.4.0.
enum_values_removed.rejection_message: target_config.cdc_load_strategy: removed in v1.4.0 -- it existed only to consume the surrogate-key engine, hashing every payload column of every row on every run to manufacture a diff key. Use FULL_SNAPSHOT_CDC with target_config.primary_keys (the Databricks-native apply_changes_from_snapshot pattern -- https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/ldp/cdc), or TRUNCATE_AND_LOAD if this source genuinely has no key to diff on.
enum_values_removed.rejection_note: Checked BEFORE the generic allowed-values test, so the author sees why the strategy was withdrawn and what replaces it, not a generic 'not one of [...]' list.

migration.situation: The source has a natural key, it was just never declared (the common case)
The source genuinely has no key

enum_values_removed.migration_warning: Verify the candidate key is actually unique in the snapshot before committing to it (SELECT k, count(*) FROM src GROUP BY k HAVING count(*) > 1). A non-unique key produces a target that looks correct and silently collapses rows.
enum_values_removed.behavioural_change: Under the removed strategy a Day-2 field change was reported as a DELETE of the old row plus an INSERT of a new one (the same entity under two identities, because the whole payload was the key). With a declared primary key that change is reported as the UPDATE it is. Expect the first post-migration snapshot to diff as a full delete-and-reinsert, because the diff key itself changed; correct behaviour thereafter.
enum_values_removed.app_action: Remove the tab/option from the CDC strategy selector. Update the asn1_snapshot ingestion preset and the snapshot transformation preset to FULL_SNAPSHOT_CDC with primary_keys.

modified.before: Required for SCD1, SCD2, SCD3, FULL_SNAPSHOT_CDC. Explicitly NOT required for FULL_SNAPSHOT_CDC_NO_PK.
modified.after: Required for SCD1, SCD2, SCD3, FULL_SNAPSHOT_CDC -- i.e. every CDC-dispatched strategy, since the keyless variant no longer exists. There is no framework-generated substitute.
modified.runtime_error_when_missing: Flow '<flow_id>': FULL_SNAPSHOT_CDC requires target_config.primary_keys -- apply_changes_from_snapshot diffs successive snapshots on a key, and as of v1.4.0 the framework no longer manufactures one. Declare the source's natural key, or switch this flow to TRUNCATE_AND_LOAD if it genuinely has none.
modified.new_runtime_guard: A primary_keys entry that never reaches the clean upstream (renamed by column_normalization, projected away by data_standardization_sql) is caught inside the snapshot-input dataset at graph-execution time and reported with the available columns.
modified.app_action: The visibility/required predicate for primary_keys must now include FULL_SNAPSHOT_CDC: ["SCD1","SCD2","SCD3","FULL_SNAPSHOT_CDC"].

modified.before: Presence-tested. An object omitting `enabled` deferred enablement to source_config.normalize_column_names, so an object supplying only `case` could be ON.
modified.after: Read with .get("enabled", False). Absent object, absent key and explicit false are all OFF. This is the only switch.
modified.app_action: The `column_normalization.case` field's visibility condition must depend on `column_normalization.enabled === true` alone.

modified.before: Valid for {SCD1, SCD2, FULL_SNAPSHOT_CDC, FULL_SNAPSHOT_CDC_NO_PK}; UI additionally excluded FULL_SNAPSHOT_CDC_NO_PK.
modified.after: Valid for {SCD1, SCD2, FULL_SNAPSHOT_CDC}. The former exclusion of the withdrawn strategy is now vacuous and must be deleted rather than left as a live-looking rule.
modified.app_action: Set the predicate to the exact set: ["SCD1","SCD2","FULL_SNAPSHOT_CDC"]. Do NOT use an isCdc(strategy) helper -- that set includes SCD3, which the validator rejects.

app_action_superseded.why: isCdc(strategy) is {SCD1, SCD2, SCD3, FULL_SNAPSHOT_CDC}, but this attribute's applicability set is {SCD1, SCD2, FULL_SNAPSHOT_CDC} -- exactly what this entry's own `after` field already said. The instruction contradicted the delta it belonged to, and the app implemented the instruction: databricks-app/web/src/Builder.jsx offered cdc_operation_column and cdc_operation_mapping.delete_values on SCD3, producing a spec the builder accepted and onboarding rejected.

modified.before: Narrowed this side's read only when recon_mode resolved to "triggered" AND the task_run_id job parameter was non-empty AND this side declared the column.
modified.after: Narrows whenever the task_run_id job parameter is non-empty AND this side declares the column. The recon_mode condition is gone with the attribute. One asymmetry is retained deliberately: in a mixed batch/streaming comparison only the STATIC side is narrowed, because the streaming side's own micro-batch offsets already are the batch boundary.
modified.app_action: Description text only -- no field shape change.

modified.clarification: It is an ASSERTION about the dataset, never an instruction to the engine. It does NOT precompute row hashes over match_keys, and it does not expect a third party's own hash column. true = 'this framework already wrote __framework_hash_key/__framework_hash_value onto this table upstream, at CDC-materialization time' -- they are trusted verbatim and match_keys/compare_columns are not hashed at all. false (default) = compute both NOW: __framework_hash_key over match_keys in the DECLARED ORDER, __framework_hash_value over the resolved compare_columns ALPHABETICALLY SORTED.
modified.hard_error_on_true_when_absent: hash_precomputed=True but dataset is missing ['__framework_hash_key', '__framework_hash_value'] -- this dataset was not actually produced by a CDC-dispatched flow with generate_hash_columns enabled (see cdc/hashing.py), so its __framework_hash_key/__framework_hash_value cannot be trusted for reconciliation matching
modified.silent_failure_mode: The precondition that makes `true` safe is that the upstream flow's primary_keys are this flow's match_keys and its resolved comparison columns are this flow's compare_columns. When they disagree NOTHING ERRORS -- the hashes simply never match and every row reports as drifted.
modified.app_action: Description/help text only -- no field shape change. Recommend wording that leads with 'already computed upstream', not 'precompute'.

modified.clarification: For a mode: "continuous" destination this is THE place the DLT event-log table list is configured -- on the observability row, part of the onboarding spec, upserted into observability_config. The pipeline-level `dataflow.otel_streaming.event_log_tables` spark configuration remains only as an explicitly subordinate BOOTSTRAP FALLBACK, consulted when the control-table lookup yields nothing. `dataflow.group.id` and `dataflow.control.catalog` correctly stay as pipeline configuration -- they are what let the pipeline find its own rows.
unchanged_rules: Rejected when mode == "triggered" (the triggered engine resolves its pipeline from the upstream task run, so the list would be silently ignored).

job_task_parameter_delta.$comment: NOT part of the onboarding spec document -- these are Lakeflow JOB task base_parameters on the observability notebook task (notebooks/08_observability/08_dlt_observability_engine.py). Included because the Databricks App and any job-authoring surface must emit them.

renamed.reason: The old name baked one convention -- a task literally called `run_pipeline_update` -- into the parameter name, so it read as a lie in every job whose pipeline task is called something else.

now_required.name: dataflow_group_id
now_required.before: derived from the upstream pipeline's dataflow.group.id
now_required.after: REQUIRED task parameter; the derived value is kept as a cross-check and a disagreement raises
now_required.reason: A derived value cannot detect depends_on pointing at the wrong pipeline_task -- whatever pipeline the task lands on reports its own group id happily, and the export succeeds while describing the wrong dataflow.

now_required.name: env
now_required.after: REQUIRED, renamed to `env`; becomes the OTel deployment.environment resource attribute
now_required.reason: Optional environment labelling is worse than none: telemetry that omits it is silently merged with every other environment's in the consumer.

pipeline_parameters_question.question: Does pipeline_task_run_id need to be declared in pipeline_parameters?
pipeline_parameters_question.answer: NO -- and it must not be.
pipeline_parameters_question.reason: {{tasks.<key>.run_id}} is a Jobs DYNAMIC VALUE REFERENCE, resolved by the Jobs service per JOB RUN at the moment the downstream task is dispatched. A pipeline's pipeline_parameters / configuration: block is resolved by the Pipelines service per PIPELINE UPDATE and is static for that deployment -- there is no job run in scope for a task value to resolve against. Declaring it there cannot work and would at best pin every run to a stale literal.
pipeline_parameters_question.rule: Dynamic, per-run values travel as task parameters. Static, per-deployment values travel as pipeline configuration.

job_task_parameter_delta.known_trap: A mistyped task key does NOT fail loudly on its own. When <key> in {{tasks.<key>.run_id}} does not name a task in the job, the Jobs service substitutes nothing and passes the literal template text through as the parameter value. observability/runtime_params.py checks for exactly that and names it.

removed.note: No longer generated by any flow. A table materialized before the upgrade still physically carries it: it is NOT dropped, cdc/comparison_columns.py still excludes it from comparison-column resolution, and storage/column_ordering.py no longer front-loads it.

control_table_delta.$comment: 01_setup only ever runs CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS, never a migration. An already-provisioned table therefore KEEPS these columns physically; they simply stop being written (they are nullable, so the MERGE inserts NULL). No migration script is required.

reconciliation_flow_spec.note: recon_mode was never written by onboarding/metadata_upsert.py in the first place -- it existed in the DDL and was read defensively via getattr by the reconciliation notebook.

python_api_delta.$comment: For any caller outside this repository.

app_update_checklist: databricks-app/config/registry/ingestion.json -- drop source_config.normalize_column_names; fix the column_normalization.case visibility condition.

databricks-app/config/registry/shared.cdc.json -- drop the FULL_SNAPSHOT_CDC_NO_PK tab and the three surrogate_key_* fields; replace the strategy in every applicability list with FULL_SNAPSHOT_CDC; delete now-vacuous `ne` guards against the withdrawn strategy.
databricks-app/config/registry/shared.target.json -- add source_data_type to the encrypted_columns[] repeat group, after `mode`.
databricks-app/config/registry/reconciliation.json + fragments.json -- drop recon_mode and generate_surrogate_key; update task_run_id_column help text.
databricks-app/config/attribute_knowledge.json -- drop the removed attribute entries, add source_data_type, fix the CDC strategy catalogue.
databricks-app/web/src/registry.js + Builder.jsx -- same deltas on the frontend; add FULL_SNAPSHOT_CDC to the primary_keys required-for list.
databricks-app/templates/**.json + index.json -- update presets; asn1_snapshot and the snapshot transformation preset move to FULL_SNAPSHOT_CDC + primary_keys.
REBUILD web/dist -- `npm install && npm run build` in databricks-app/web. Databricks Apps does not build at deploy time, so an un-rebuilt bundle keeps offering fields the framework now rejects.
Spec IMPORT path -- surface a removed attribute as a migration warning rather than silently preserving or dropping it.

app_surface_corrections.$comment: Defects found on 2026-08-30 by re-verifying the v1.4.0 app pass against the framework validator itself rather than against this document. Each was a disagreement between what the app offers or ships and what onboarding/spec_validator.py accepts. Listed here so an agent replaying this delta does not reintroduce them.
app_surface_corrections.verification_method: databricks-app/tests/test_framework_spec_agreement.py imports the real validate_spec and drives every shipped template and every (strategy x optional attribute) pair through it.

corrections.symptom: cdc_operation_column / cdc_operation_mapping.delete_values were offered on SCD3, which onboarding rejects.
corrections.fix: New hasDeleteMarker(s) helper = {SCD1, SCD2, FULL_SNAPSHOT_CDC}, replacing isCdc in both field predicates; registry visible_when set to the same list.

corrections.symptom: Removing the FULL_SNAPSHOT_CDC_NO_PK guard left a one-argument predicate {"ne": ["target_config.cdc_load_strategy"]} behind. evaluate_predicate reaches its binary operators behind len(args) >= 2 and otherwise returns False, so both delete-marker fields were invisible for EVERY strategy in the registry-driven surface -- silently, no error.
corrections.fix: Predicate deleted. A test now rejects any binary operator with fewer than two operands anywhere in config/registry/*.json.

corrections.symptom: scd_requires_primary_keys still listed only [SCD1, SCD2, SCD3], so a FULL_SNAPSHOT_CDC flow with no primary_keys passed the app's own validator and failed onboarding. This is the app_action of modified[0], which was never applied to rules.json.
corrections.fix: FULL_SNAPSHOT_CDC added to the rule's strategy list and to its message.

corrections.symptom: columns_to_exclude_cdc_only fired only on APPEND and TRUNCATE_AND_LOAD; the framework rejects the attribute on FULL_SNAPSHOT_CDC too.
corrections.fix: Rule restated as the complement of the strategies that HAVE a comparison concept: nin [SCD1, SCD2, SCD3], so a future strategy cannot fall through it.

corrections.symptom: sink_config.format offered "kafka", but no field existed for kafka_options -- which the framework requires, and which must carry both kafka.bootstrap.servers and topic. A kafka sink could not be authored in the app at all.
corrections.fix: kafka_options added as a kv field, visible when format == kafka. kafka_secret_options (a map of option name to secret ref) remains unauthorable -- the serializer has no repeat-to-map-of-secretRef shape -- and is now named explicitly in the field's help text as hand-edit-only.

corrections.symptom: Flow rule contexts exposed only `v` (flat scalars), so any rule referencing a kv or repeat path resolved to None whether populated or not -- an `empty` guard on one would fire on a correctly-filled flow.
corrections.fix: resolve_path_value falls back to context['kvs'] / context['reps']; both flow contexts now carry them.

corrections.symptom: Shipped the builder's decomposed target keys (target_catalog / target_schema / target_table) instead of the canonical three-part `table` the framework reads. It round-trips through the builder, but is rejected if saved as written -- and the two sibling reconciliation templates already used the canonical shape.
corrections.fix: Rewritten to {type, table}. Every shipped template is now driven through the real validator by a test.

corrections.symptom: reconciliation transform_sql read FROM missing_records -- a view nothing creates. The appender registers the miss set as _reconciliation_unmatched_records (appender.py::UNMATCHED_RECORDS_VIEW_NAME). The app's copy and both full-reference documents were already correct; only this pair was stale.
corrections.fix: Both files corrected; a test now asserts the app and framework copies are identical.

corrections.symptom: Described columns_to_check / columns_to_exclude / cdc_operation_column as 'common optional target_config fields across every CDC-dispatched strategy'. Two of the three are narrower, so an agent following the skill emitted specs onboarding rejects.
corrections.fix: Replaced with a per-field valid-for / rejected-on table naming the two enforcing sets in spec_validator.py. A new SKILL.md section 9.1 documents encrypted_columns[].source_data_type, the one attribute this delta ADDS, which the skill had not covered.

corrections.symptom: Three optional attributes the framework validates were unauthorable in the app: post_export_archive.export_file_name_format, post_export_archive.pgp_encryption.sign_passphrase_secret, and pre_extraction_decryption.passphrase_secret (the PGP private key's own passphrase, which is a different key from secret_passphrase, the ZIP archive's AES password).
corrections.fix: All three added, with help text spelling out the passphrase_secret / secret_passphrase distinction on both fields.
